messages.text: Delap's chance at redemption against toothless Chelsea

metadata.summary: When Liam Delap joined Chelsea in the summer of 2025, he probably had ambitions of cementing himself as an elite Premier League No 9. Perhaps even positioning himself to be the heir to Harry Kane's throne for England.
metadata.content: Liam Delap has a chance to show Chelsea what they're missing when they travel to Nottingham Forest | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Liam Delap has a chance to show Chelsea what they're missing when they travel to Nottingham Forest Liam Delap has a chance to show former club Chelsea what they are missing as Xabi Alonso's side continue to struggle in attack without Joao Pedro; watch Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea live on Sky Sports Premier League and Main Event on Friday Night Football; kick-off 8pm Callum Bishop Football Journalist Wednesday 25 November 2026 12:17, UK When Liam Delap joined Chelsea in the summer of 2025, he probably had ambitions of cementing himself as an elite Premier League No 9. Perhaps even positioning himself to be the heir to Harry Kane's throne for England. Less than a month later, Joao Pedro made the move to Stamford Bridge and suddenly, the landscape changed. He was not the first-choice striker at the club. What followed was an arduous campaign that brought three goals in 47 games and saw Delap succumb to what is now the fabled curse of the Chelsea No 9 shirt. A club-record move to Nottingham Forest in August has yet to truly revitalise his career either. But Oliver Glasner does have faith that there's a 20-goal-a-season striker hiding in the 23-year-old. messages.text: Bearman confirmed to stay at Haas for 2027

metadata.summary: Haas have confirmed Oliver Bearman will stay at the team for the 2027 Formula 1 season, after protracted contract talks resulted in a one-year extension.
metadata.content: Oliver Bearman to remain with Haas for 2027 F1 season after new contract finally agreed ahead of Qatar GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Oliver Bearman to remain with Haas for 2027 F1 season after new contract finally agreed ahead of Qatar GP Oliver Bearman has signed a one-year contract extension to remain with Haas for the 2027 F1 season; watch the Qatar GP on Sky Sports F1 this weekend, with qualifying at 6pm on Saturday and the race at 4pm on Sunday Thursday 26 November 2026 09:09, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oliver Bearman had previously shared his frustration at the delay in confirmation of his future at Haas. Haas have confirmed Oliver Bearman will stay at the team for the 2027 Formula 1 season, after protracted contract talks resulted in a one-year extension. Despite both the British driver and American-owned team having repeatedly insisted they wanted to continue together, negotiations had dragged on for several months, leading to speculation that his links to Ferrari - who he remains tied to after coming through their academy - were a factor in the delay. The 21-year-old said ahead of last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix that he was "disappointed" a resolution had not been found, but the wait for confirmation was finally ended by Haas on Thursday ahead of this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix. It was a nightmare performance for Lammens, who unnecessarily conceded a penalty for Luis Suarez's opener just 75 seconds after saving the Sporting striker's poorly taken first spot-kick. Lammens, 24, then spilt a routine cross late in the second half, allowing Suarez to equalise for 2-2 and denying United their first away win of the season and their first Champions League win on the road in five years. White-ball captain Harry Brook is flying home before the fifth and final T20 against Australia next Wednesday, while regular deputy Will Jacks has been ruled out of the rest of the series due to a broken hand.
